What the system is meant to do

Bring a small RISC-V core together with neural-network accelerators and data movement for edge anomaly-detection workloads. This is an active student ASIC effort led through the Chip Designers Guild at VIT Chennai.

Current architecture description

  • Ibex RV32IM CPU core.
  • INT8 neural processing unit with 64 MACs.
  • 256-neuron LIF spiking neural network accelerator.
  • Four-channel DMA and Wishbone interconnect.

The SCL180 process is the target. The architecture and student implementation work are in active development; this page does not imply tapeout or measured silicon.

My role

As founder and captain of the Guild, I coordinate RTL, verification, FPGA prototyping and ASIC-flow work. The project is also a team learning exercise in integration: interfaces, memory movement, reset behavior, and reproducible tests matter as much as the accelerator blocks.

Next evidence to publish

Once available, publish a stable regression summary, FPGA demonstration, and an implementation report detailing the exact RTL revision, tool versions, constraints, and PDK assumptions.
